title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement: Given a string, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. Use a sliding window with a hash set to track characters currently in the window.

title: Minimum Window Substring
statement: Given two strings s and t, find the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included in the window. Return an empty string if no such window exists.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement: Given an array and a sliding window of size k moving from left to right, return the maximum value in each window. Use a monotonic deque to maintain candidates efficiently.

title: Fruit Into Baskets
statement: Given an array representing fruit types on a tree, find the length of the longest subarray containing at most two distinct fruit types, simulating picking fruit into two baskets.

title: Max Consecutive Ones III
statement: Given a binary array and an integer k, return the maximum number of consecutive 1s if you can flip at most k zeros to ones using a sliding window.

title: Permutation in String
statement: Given two strings s1 and s2, return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1 as a contiguous substring, using a fixed-size sliding window and character frequency counts.

title: Binary Search
statement: Given a sorted array of integers and a target value, return the index of the target if it exists, otherwise return -1, using classic binary search in O(log n) time.

title: Search Insert Position
statement: Given a sorted array and a target value, return the index if found, or the index where it would be inserted to keep the array sorted, in O(log n) time.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
statement: Given a rotated sorted array with unique elements and a target, search for the target in O(log n) time by determining which half of the array is properly sorted at each step.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
statement: Given a rotated sorted array with no duplicates, find the minimum element in O(log n) time by comparing midpoint values against the array's endpoints.

title: Koko Eating Bananas
statement: Given piles of bananas and a number of hours, find the minimum eating speed k such that Koko can eat all bananas within the time limit, using binary search on the answer.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
statement: Given two sorted arrays of different sizes, find the median of the combined array in O(log(min(m,n))) time using a binary search partition approach.

title: Number of Islands
statement: Given a 2D grid of '1's (land) and '0's (water), count the number of islands, where an island is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically, using DFS or BFS.

title: Course Schedule
statement: Given a number of courses and a list of prerequisite pairs, determine if it's possible to finish all courses, which is equivalent to detecting a cycle in a directed graph.

title: Rotting Oranges
statement: Given a grid of fresh, rotten, and empty cells, find the minimum time for all fresh oranges to rot, where rot spreads to adjacent cells each minute, using multi-source BFS.

title: Word Ladder
statement: Given a begin word, an end word, and a word list, find the length of the shortest transformation sequence changing one letter at a time, where each intermediate word must exist in the list, using BFS.

title: Network Delay Time
statement: Given a network of nodes with weighted directed edges and a starting node, find the minimum time for a signal to reach all nodes, using Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm.

title: Redundant Connection
statement: Given a graph that started as a tree with one extra edge added, find the edge that can be removed to restore it to a tree, using Union-Find to detect the cycle-causing edge.

title: Climbing Stairs
statement: Given n steps, where you can climb 1 or 2 steps at a time, count the number of distinct ways to reach the top, which follows a Fibonacci-like recurrence.

title: House Robber
statement: Given an array of house values, find the maximum amount that can be robbed without robbing two adjacent houses, using DP where each state depends on the previous two.

title: Coin Change
statement: Given coin denominations and a target amount, find the minimum number of coins needed to make that amount, or -1 if it's not possible, using bottom-up DP.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement: Given an integer array, find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence, solvable in O(n^2) DP or O(n log n) with binary search.

title: Edit Distance
statement: Given two strings, find the minimum number of insert, delete, or replace operations required to convert one string into the other, using 2D DP over string prefixes.

title: Burst Balloons
statement: Given balloons with values, where bursting a balloon earns coins equal to the product of its neighbors' values, find the maximum coins obtainable by bursting all balloons in some order, using interval DP.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth, defined as the number of nodes along the longest path from root to the farthest leaf.

title: Invert Binary Tree
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, invert it so that it becomes its own mirror image, by recursively swapping the left and right children of every node.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the values of its nodes grouped level by level, from left to right, using BFS with a queue.

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the diameter, defined as the longest path between any two nodes, which may or may not pass through the root.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree, where every node's value falls within a valid range determined by its ancestors.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
statement: Design an algorithm to serialize a binary tree into a string and deserialize that string back into the original tree structure, preserving all node values and structure.

title: Two Sum
statement: Given an array of integers and a target sum, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target, using a hash map for O(n) time.

title: Contains Duplicate
statement: Given an integer array, return true if any value appears at least twice, using a hash set to track seen elements in a single pass.

title: Product of Array Except Self
statement: Given an array, return an array where each element is the product of all other elements except itself, without using division, using prefix and suffix products.

title: Maximum Subarray
statement: Given an integer array, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum, using Kadane's algorithm in O(n) time.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
statement: Given an unsorted array of integers, find the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers, achievable in O(n) time using a hash set.

title: Trapping Rain Water
statement: Given an array representing elevation heights, compute how much water can be trapped between the bars after raining, using two pointers or prefix max arrays.
